body:
The functionality from this PR: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/96740 seems to be broken. Looks like it's not filtering out the RID for the selected node anymore and repositioning it over itself. 

Default Physics in a build with this PR / Jolt as an extension: 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/70b0dd55-b965-48fb-a3cf-ae8b68d2d33e

Jolt in this PR:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bae33d8f-7b58-49ec-8652-2734658343f8

Absolutely great work @mihe and @jrouwe !

Remember this exchange on the RocketChat #physics channel?

![godot-jolt-beginning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05f45a2d-88ff-43dd-b69e-0e4ca4e91a46)

Nice progress so far. I have just some minor review comments, but other than that I think this looks good to merge for wider user testing.

Tested again wit the new fixes and now did not manage to crash with jolt, even with multi-threaded physics.

The crash before is now error spam when the jolt numbers get exhausted, e.g. with the Godot physics demo performance tests. I think we need to make that error only print once to users instead of spamming it as it "feels" like a crash when the editor starts to print so many errors endlessly.

Godot physics crashed 3 times in my tests and did not even manage to load the test scene with multi-threading enabled. So I think even with some unfinished edges the jolt module is already in a better state and largely an improvement over what is available in master.

From a usage point I think this module would be already good and stable enough to give it to users for testing in one of the pre-releases to find more subtle bugs.

Did not do a code review.
(I got scared by the file count)

I've tested a few various scenarios, including adjusting project settings using https://github.com/Open-Industry-Project/Open-Industry-Project which heavily relies on physics and haven't run into any real issues. Seems to work pretty much like the add-on. Excited for this to be part of the engine, couldn't have done it without Jolt.

Tested locally, it works as expected on all 3D demos from https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects **except** the 3D physics tests demo which crashes on startup (see below). I've tested both `precision=single` and `precision=double` builds, including when I moved the world 10 billion units away from the origin. I've also tested various physics ticks per second values and they all work correctly, including physics interpolation.

Some feedback:

- The **Bounce Velocity Threshold** and **Sleep Velocity Threshold** project settings are missing range hints, as they shouldn't be allowed to be negative (or even zero, perhaps):

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fee9c661-cd51-413f-8379-318d476dbb53)

- The [3D Physics Tests](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/master/3d/physics_tests) demo crashes on startup, likely because of debug collision shape drawing. This doesn't occur on 4.4.dev5.

I've reviewed the thirdparty code integration, and skimmed through some of the module code, this is very solid work.

The code style seems pretty good, I could find some nitpicks but not really worth pointing out on such a massive code conversion from extension to module.

Tested briefly with the GDQuest 3D TPS demo, it seems to work well as a drop-in replacement.

I would suggest making the project setting for the physics engine a "basic" setting so it's easy to find for users who want to test Jolt. And for good measure the 2D one can likely be too, since there are some GDExtensions available for Box2D and Rapier2D I believe.
